hypothesis: Writer identity across scripts may be better represented by both the average activation pattern and the spatial variability of high-level handwriting features than by spatial means alone.
candidate_representation: L2-normalized 512-D spatial mean plus independently L2-normalized 512-D spatial standard deviation, concatenated and L2-normalized to 1024-D
mean_std_weighting: Equal contribution after independent L2 normalization
useful_auc_gain: style descriptor minus raw embedding macro AUC >= 0.01
strong_auc_gain: style descriptor minus raw embedding macro AUC >= 0.03
useful_eer_reduction: pooled EER decreases by at least 0.01 absolute

interpretation_cases.strong_support: At least one encoder gains >= 0.03 macro AUC, does not materially worsen pooled EER, and improves at least 3 of 4 cross-script conditions.
interpretation_cases.promising_support: At least one encoder gains >= 0.01 but less than 0.03 macro AUC.
interpretation_cases.eer_only_signal: Macro AUC gain is below 0.01 but pooled EER improves by at least 0.01 absolute.
interpretation_cases.no_meaningful_support: Neither encoder shows useful AUC gain or useful EER reduction.
interpretation_cases.harmful: Mean-plus-std decreases macro AUC for both encoders without a useful pooled EER reduction.
